brief:
**BLUF:** No major incidents, alerts or emergencies reported in Tazewell County or the immediate core area on Sunday, November 1. Recent developments include a $2.1 million federal road safety grant for Tazewell County corridors and the upcoming launch of a school attendance communication tool on November 4. In the broader region, West Virginia allocated $2 million in Rural Health Transformation funds to community health centers.[[1]](https://www.bdtonline.com/news/griffith-announces-more-than-2-1-million-dot-public-safety-grant-to-tazewell-county/article_3267cf81-712b-4cc5-8589-7df851ed6a3f.html)[[2]](https://www.bdtonline.com/news/tazewell-county-public-schools-to-launch-attendance-assistant/article_2b6a18f3-d5fc-438d-9cf2-ed1858dff3e8.html)

## LAW ENFORCEMENT AND COURTS
Nothing reported in the last 24 hours.

## FIRE, EMS AND RESCUE
Nothing reported in the last 24 hours.

## HAZARDS, WEATHER AND ROADS
Nothing reported in the last 24 hours. A bridge rehabilitation project continues on the Frank S. Easley Bridge (U.S. Route 52) in Bluefield, WV, with two-way traffic maintained, a reduced 25 mph speed limit in the work zone, and double fines for violations; completion expected by spring.[[3]](https://wvpress.org/breaking-news/major-bridge-rehabilitation-project-underway-in-bluefield/)

## GOVERNMENT AND POLITICS
Tazewell County Public Schools will launch an “attendance assistant” text-based tool on November 4 in partnership with Edia Learning to help families report absences and submit documentation.[[2]](https://www.bdtonline.com/news/tazewell-county-public-schools-to-launch-attendance-assistant/article_2b6a18f3-d5fc-438d-9cf2-ed1858dff3e8.html)

U.S. Rep. Morgan Griffith announced a $2,118,842 U.S. Department of Transportation grant to Tazewell County for safety improvements (double centerline striping, rumble strips, high-friction surfaces, signs and transition zones) on six high-risk rural corridors: Jewell Ridge Road, Falls Mills Road, Baptist Valley Road, Wardell Road, Indian Creek Road and Kents Ridge Road.[[1]](https://www.bdtonline.com/news/griffith-announces-more-than-2-1-million-dot-public-safety-grant-to-tazewell-county/article_3267cf81-712b-4cc5-8589-7df851ed6a3f.html)

Tazewell County is purchasing property near Cavitts Creek Park (house and 12 acres) for approximately $460,000 using opioid settlement funds to establish a women’s addiction recovery residence (up to 12–15 women) operated by A Hope and Future Ministry, with a target opening by the end of 2026.[[4]](https://cardinalnews.org/2026/10/28/womens-addiction-recovery-residence-set-to-open-in-tazewell-county-by-the-end-of-the-year/)

## ECONOMY AND OTHER
Bluefield Parks and Recreation hosted its annual Trunk or Treat event at City Park on October 31.[[5]](https://www.wvva.com/news/)

Princeton Senior High cheerleaders hosted a car show on October 31 to raise funds for a trip to nationals.[[6]](https://www.wvva.com)

The American Red Cross will hold a blood drive at Bluefield, VA Town Hall on Thursday, November 5.[[7]](https://www.bdtonline.com/)

West Virginia is distributing more than $2 million in federal Rural Health Transformation program funds to community health centers statewide.[[8]](https://muckrack.com/media-outlet/bdtonline)

## WATCH -- NEXT 48 HOURS
- November 4: Tazewell County Public Schools attendance assistant tool launches.
- November 5: Blood drive at Bluefield, VA Town Hall.
- Ongoing: Early voting concluded October 31; general election November 3 in Virginia and West Virginia. Bridge work on U.S. 52 in Bluefield, WV.
